transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Time: 10:00am PT
Duration: ~40 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Tom (Cascade PM), Maya (Cascade ML), Liam (Cascade Security)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call  Jordan Ellis here from Redwood, Priya is with me, and we good to kick?
[00:10] Priya: Yep, Priya on the line. I pulled the eval spreadsheet you sent, trying to get an idea of the regression numbers.
[00:18] Tom: Tom here. Quick note, we have about 40 minutes today. We want to make sure we lock the prompt changes and the guardrails for the next run.
[00:25] Maya: Maya joining, sorry for the slight delay, internal deploy churn.
[00:30] Liam: Liam from security  will listen in and ask KMS/VPC questions at the end.

Summary & context
[00:45] Jordan: Recap: last week we rolled out prompt set v3 and a small reranking tweak. The Redwood Optimize suggestions were applied  auto-batching was left off to keep latency stable. We saw a small drop in precision on the negative-qa set, so this week is about diagnosing regressions and choosing which prompts to keep.

Eval review (results walkthrough)
[01:30] Priya: I have the sheet up. Overall aggregate score stayed at 0.83 to two decimals, but if you split by intent, Search intent down from 0.88 to 0.82, and Summarization up a touch. The false-positive rate increased on the policy guardrail tests.
[02:05] Tom: Can you clarify "policy guardrail tests"  is that the toxicity filtering or the business logic guardrail?
[02:12] Priya: A little bit of both  we run the outputs through our rule set plus the heuristic toxicity filter. Some prompts in v3 are producing more verbose answers that accidentally trip heuristics.
[02:23] Maya: Right, we saw that in the batch sample  some system prompts with the new context expansion create extra phrasing that the filter flags. Might be wording sensitivity.

[03:00] Jordan: Important to note transcription may be spotty in the automated notes, sorry  e.g., Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as "Redwood Dedicate" in the sheet, so ignore small naming typos.

Prompt tuning & guardrails discussion
[03:30] Priya: Proposed fix: add an explicit system instruction to constrain verbosity for the Search intent prompts, and tighten the reranker threshold for the top-3 candidates. That should reduce spurious heuristic trips without hurting Summarization.
[04:10] Tom: What's the risk of harming recall by tightening the reranker? We care about not missing relevant results.
[04:18] Priya: Good point. We can reduce threshold incrementally and run ablation across 500 samples to measure recall drop. We recommend a conservative change first  delta from 0.55 to 0.5 threshold, then rollout to 10% of traffic in the POC.

Regression plan and metrics
[05:00] Priya: For regression, we propose: holdout 5k labeled examples, run v2 (baseline) vs v3 + guardrail changes, compute per-intent precision/recall, average human rating, and failure modes count. Also flag any outputs that change categories (e.g. safe -> unsafe).
[05:40] Maya: We have 8k labeled samples but only 3k with intent granularity  I'll push label mappings to you. We should be careful about class imbalance.
[05:55] Jordan: Perfect  that's an action item for Maya. Also, do we want to add automated diffing by output token-level changes? Redwood has an eval hook that does approximate token-diff and highlights regenerated segments.
[06:15] Tom: That'd be useful to triage. If the model just rephrased the same answer, we probably don't call it a regression.

Scoring rubric & human rating workflow
[06:40] Priya: Scoring rubric: 1-5 human rating on relevance and factuality; separate binary flag for policy violation. We'll attach annotation examples in the rubric. Also include a confidence band so we can prioritize human reviews on low-confidence/high-impact queries.
[07:10] Jordan: Note that automated scoring currently uses a hybrid of embedding similarity and a lightweight safety classifier. Humans should review disagreements > 0.3 embedding distance.

Noise / transcription issues (realistic imperfections)
[07:45] Speaker 1: [inaudible] I think the redwood price -- sorry -- Redwood price bang cut.
[07:55] Priya: There's some background there, can you repeat?
[08:02] Tom: I said we need the cost numbers to show to procurement; can you give a hosted vs dedicated estimate for the pilot?

Latency & cost tradeoffs (benchmarks)
[08:20] Priya: For the pilot at our observed QPS, hosted latency median is ~220ms per token on the curated model, Dedicated would be ~120ms with batching but cost per token drops ~30-40% once you hit reserved capacity. Those are rough  I'll run a 10k token batch test and share the numbers.
[08:50] Maya: Is that factoring quantization profiles? We plan to try int8 via Redwood Optimize.
[08:57] Priya: Not fully  the 120ms estimate assumed mixed precision. Quantization to int8 can shave 10-25% more, but we need to verify output quality for Summarization intents.

Security & deployment constraints
[09:25] Liam: Quick security callouts: KMS/HSM integration required for keys, we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and VPC peering for Private deployment is likely. Also SOC2 artifacts and pen-test reports are requested by our compliance team.
[09:45] Jordan: All standard  we'll share the security pack and SOC2 report. For KMS we support both customer-managed KMS via Redwood Private and key wrapping for Dedicated. I'll add the security playbook link to the follow-ups.

Open questions and edge cases
[10:20] Tom: A couple edge cases  long legal passages where we want verbatim citations; how does the reranker treat citation fidelity?
[10:30] Priya: If you need verbatim citation, we can add a citation-preserve flag to the prompt; reranker will then boost candidates that include exact spans. That does slightly reduce diversity.
[10:45] Maya: Also, we observed hallucination on rare entity types (product SKUs). Can we add a KB retrieval step?
[10:53] Jordan: Yes, we can integrate a retrieval layer and use Redwood API to condition on top-k docs. That would increase latency a bit but reduce hallucination.

Middle of call - triage examples live
[11:30] Priya: I pulled three failing examples: Example A - baseline ok, v3 returns extra recommendation that trips policy; Example B - summarization trimmed critical detail; Example C - search returns lower relevance.
[12:00] Tom: For Example A, can we show the exact prompt and output in the sheet?
[12:08] Priya: Done, added a snippet. Note the system prompt had a new "be helpful and expansive" line which caused verbosity.
[12:25] Maya: Suggest changing that line to "be concise and prioritize relevant facts" for Search.

Rollout strategy discussion
[13:00] Jordan: Proposed rollout: fix prompts -> run 5k regression -> if pass, canary 10% traffic for 48 hours -> expand. If we see drop in recall >2% or any safety regression, rollback.
[13:25] Tom: Canary sounds good. We also want a regression dashboard that alerts on per-intent drops.
[13:35] Priya: Redwood Console can track per-route and per-model metrics; we can add triggers on those deltas and tie to an automatic fallback to previous model or to a smaller-safe model variant.

Benchmarks & timing
[14:00] Priya: Timeline: Jordan sends prompt set + rubric by 4/24; Cascade runs regression 4/24-4/28; latency benchmark 4/29; canary 5/1 pending results. Is that realistic?
[14:20] Maya: Yes, that works for us, assuming we get the label mapping quickly.

Security follow-up specifics
[14:40] Liam: On KMS: do you support customer-managed keys in Dedicated? How do we get audit logs?
[14:48] Jordan: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS with key rotation policy. Audit logs can be exported as syslog or to S3; we'll provide examples. I'll send the security pack with specifics.

Wrap up and recap
[15:10] Jordan: Quick recap: 1) We will update prompt set to constrain verbosity for Search; 2) Priya to run batch latency/cost tests; 3) Maya to provide holdout + label map; 4) Liam to confirm KMS/VPC needs. Next sync same time next week unless something urgent pops up.
[15:35] Tom: One more: can you include an example JSON of the canary routing policy? Our infra team wants config to test on our side.
[15:45] Priya: Yes I have a template, will share as part of the follow-up.

Closing noise & misc
[16:00] Speaker 1: [crosstalk] we good?
[16:05] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[16:10] Meeting end.
